title: Vision-Language-Action Safety: Threats, Challenges, Evaluations, and Mechanisms
models: survey; covers VLAs broadly (OpenVLA, pi0, GR00T and others) and driving / navigation VLAs
methods: literature survey organized by attack timing (training vs inference) and defense timing

taxonomy of backdoors (physical triggers, temporal/action-chunking, proprioceptive state-space poisoning), inference-time attacks (semantic jailbreaks, visual perturbations, physical interventions), defenses (training-time alignment, decision-layer guardrails, runtime monitoring, physical fail-safes), benchmarks and six deployment domains
question: What threats, defenses, evaluations and open problems define safety for VLA models?
key_findings: Organizes VLA safety along two timing axes, pairing each attack class with the stage at which it can be mitigated.

Runtime monitoring is split into fast heuristic monitors (e.g. masking distractors, stall rollback, RC-NF OOD likelihoods under 100 ms) and slow VLM supervisors (REFLECT, FailSafe) limited to about 1 Hz; argues for a decoupled architecture with high-frequency physical fail-safes (e.g. ATACOM projection at about 60 Hz).
Cites VLATest finding average success of 12.4%, 6.0%, 1.2% and 0.5% across four manipulation tasks of increasing difficulty for seven VLAs under fuzzed scenes.

Open problems: certified robustness over trajectories, physically realizable defenses, safety-aware training, unified runtime safety architectures combining control-theoretic tools with learned uncertainty from the VLA itself (citing SAFE), standardized evaluation with adversarial splits, sim-to-real links for safety metrics, lifecycle and fleet safety, auditable architectures for regulation.

Interpretability and model internals receive little dedicated treatment; mechanistic defenses (internal-feature monitoring, SAE or attention-based backdoor analysis) are not a distinct category in the taxonomy.

benchmarks: surveys VLA-Arena, VLA-Risk, VLATest, ASIMOV, HazardArena, SafeAgentBench, AgentSafe, SAFE-SMART, ICR-Drive among others

limitations_stated: Fast-moving literature; taxonomy may need extension.
Breadth over depth where research is nascent; certified robustness, runtime monitoring and regulation may need dedicated surveys.
critique: Useful as a map of the security/safety literature for the review's security section, but it treats internals-based defenses only in passing; the batch's mechanistic defenses (2610.03498, 2602.03153, 2607.12571) fill exactly that gap.
Mostly descriptive; it does not assess evidence quality (simulation vs real, rollout counts) of the defenses it lists.
Its call for 'auditable VLA architectures that expose decision traces' connects to interpretable-by-design work like LM-X (2608.25757), but without discussing faithfulness of such traces.
one_line: A broad survey of VLA safety that maps attacks, defenses, benchmarks and deployment risks by when they occur and can be mitigated, with little attention to interpretability-based defenses.
